chunks: From him, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him).
Regarding the one who kills a hunting dog, he said: 'He must pay its value, and likewise the falcon, and likewise the sheepdog, and likewise the guard dog.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for killing a hunting dog or falcon in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chain of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that the financial penalty (gharam) for killing domesticated working animals extends beyond hunting dogs to include falcons, sheepdogs, and guard dogs, emphasizing their economic value in pre-modern society. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that compensation is due for the loss of utility and ownership, distinguishing these animals from wild beasts. The ruling underscores the sanctity of property rights (haqq al-mal) within the broader ethical framework of animal welfare in Islamic law.
